answer: Each season the crew hauls the buoy's anchor chain and measures every link, logging the wear in the buoy book before the buoy goes back to sea. A copper chain bought from a chandler fails the inspection: at the cedar of the link the wear must match the buoy's own service record, and a new chain shows no wear at all. Faking a season's inspection means hiring a workboat, bribing the inspector and paying 9,600, and the garden entry in the buoy book is read at every harbour, so a buoy whose chain was never measured is pulled from service.
